From this point the corridor swings diagonally to the southeast to the Airport entrance road. It traverses agricultural type lands currently zoned for industrial use and held by the City of Milwaukee. Between 6th and 3rd Streets this corridor would cut up the City of Milwaukee's land bank area and require several newly constructed industrial buildings. Presently the north-south property lines are approximately 1/2 mile apart and abut Edgerton Avenue as well as Grange Avenue. East of 3rd Street the corridor would sever the commercial properties that abut both Howell Avenue and 3rd Street. At Howell Avenue the corridor would displace two motels and a business complex.
According to airport officials the east end of this corridor, before it crosses Howell Avenue, would be directly under the landing path of the southwest runway located north of the Air Terminal. The Federal Aviation Administration glide slope-highway clearance requirements would necessitate constructing the freeway under Howell Avenue. This corridor would therefore conflict with present plans for the air terminal expansion program in relocating passenger loading and ticket operations to the second level of the air terminal.
The length of corridor #4 from the center of existing I-S4 to a point east of Howell Avenue would be 1.65 miles.
Since a large number of residential units exist near I-94 and 6th Street, it is estimated that a freeway facility in this corridor would displace 230 people from 62 housing units. There would also be 5 commercial parcels displaced.
